subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A scalar quantity is described by which of the following?
questions.explain: A scalar has magnitude only, whereas a vector has both magnitude and direction.

questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the weight of an object?
questions.explain: Weight W = mg, where g is the gravitational field strength in N/kg.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explain: Force is measured in newtons, named after Isaac Newton.

questions.q: What is the unit of the moment of a force?
questions.explain: A moment equals force multiplied by perpendicular distance, giving units of newton metre.

questions.q: Which equation defines pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure p = F/A, the force acting normally per unit area.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of pressure?
questions.explain: One pascal is equal to one newton per square metre (1 Pa = 1 N/m²).

questions.q: Which statement expresses Hooke's law?
options: The extension is directly proportional to the force applied, up to the limit of proportionality
The extension is inversely proportional to the force applied
The extension is proportional to the square of the force applied
The extension is independent of the force applied
questions.explain: Hooke's law states F = ke, so extension is proportional to force until the limit of proportionality is reached.

questions.q: According to the principle of moments, when an object is balanced about a pivot:
options: the sum of the clockwise moments equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments
the clockwise moments are always greater than the anticlockwise moments
the total force is zero but the moments can differ
the pivot must be at the centre of the object
questions.explain: For an object in equilibrium, total clockwise moments equal total anticlockwise moments about the pivot.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explain: Velocity has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector; the others are scalars.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-contact force?
questions.explain: Gravity acts between objects without them touching, making it a non-contact force.

questions.q: If the resultant force on a moving object is zero, the object will:
options: continue moving at a constant velocity
questions.explain: With zero resultant force there is no acceleration, so the object keeps a constant velocity (Newton's first law).

questions.q: As the depth below the surface of a liquid increases, the pressure due to the liquid:
questions.explain: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth because there is a greater weight of liquid above (p = hρg).

questions.q: When a small driving gear turns a larger gear, the larger gear:
options: turns more slowly but exerts a greater moment
turns faster and exerts a greater moment
turns more slowly and exerts a smaller moment
turns at the same speed with the same moment
questions.explain: A larger gear rotates more slowly than the smaller driving gear but transmits a greater turning effect (moment).

questions.q: How does a lever make it easier to lift a heavy load?
options: The effort acts at a greater distance from the pivot, producing a larger moment
It reduces the weight of the load
It removes the need for a pivot
It increases the mass of the effort
questions.explain: A lever is a force multiplier: applying effort far from the pivot creates a large moment to overcome the load.

questions.q: Inelastic (plastic) deformation of a material means that it:
options: does not return to its original shape when the force is removed
returns exactly to its original shape when the force is removed
cannot be deformed by any force
questions.explain: Inelastic deformation is permanent, unlike elastic deformation where the object returns to its original shape.

questions.q: On a force-extension graph for a spring, the straight-line region shows that:
options: force is directly proportional to extension
force is inversely proportional to extension
the spring has passed its elastic limit
questions.explain: A linear force-extension graph indicates Hooke's law is obeyed, with force proportional to extension.

questions.q: An object has a mass of 5 kg. Taking g = 9.8 N/kg, what is its weight?
questions.explain: Weight = mass × g = 5 × 9.8 = 49 N.

questions.q: A force of 20 N acts at a perpendicular distance of 0.5 m from a pivot. What is the moment?
questions.explain: Moment = force × perpendicular distance = 20 × 0.5 = 10 Nm.

questions.q: A force of 200 N acts on a surface of area 4 m². What is the pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure = force ÷ area = 200 ÷ 4 = 50 Pa.

questions.q: A point is 2 m below the surface of water (density 1000 kg/m³, g = 9.8 N/kg). What is the pressure due to the water?
questions.explain: Pressure = hρg = 2 × 1000 × 9.8 = 19 600 Pa.
